A LITTLE ABOUT ME

✳

I like the space between
“what if” and “it works.”

I'm Emilie (Liuying) Chen, an MSc student in Applied Computational Science and Engineering at Imperial College London, with a BEng in Information Engineering from Shanghai University.

My work moves between optimization, machine learning and control. Beyond the equations, I build web projects, explore places with a camera, and look for ideas in unexpected corners.

02 — QUESTIONS WORTH ASKING

Research & recognition.

Finding structure in complexity.
One model at a time.

01

OPTIMIZATION · CO-FIRST AUTHOR

Research on Production Decision Making Based on Genetic Algorithm

Genetic algorithms, 0–1 integer programming, and dynamic programming for multi-stage production decisions.

Research overview

This work models inspection and disassembly decisions in electronics assembly, balancing production cost and defect rate. A genetic algorithm searches decision combinations, while dynamic programming evaluates the production process. Stress tests and sensitivity analysis examine robustness.

Liuying Chen, Yi Chen, Jiahao Wang · Equal contribution

Optimization
02

CONTROL · IEEE ICUS 2025 · CO-AUTHOR

Trajectory Tracking and Attitude-Constrained Control of a Tilting-Rotor Quadrotor via Linear Model Predictive Control

A linear MPC approach to trajectory tracking and attitude suppression for a tilting-rotor UAV.

Research overview

A six-degree-of-freedom nonlinear model describes a single-axis tilting-rotor quadrotor. The linear model predictive controller jointly addresses trajectory tracking and attitude constraints, exploring more precise motion with smaller posture changes.

Yuteng Huang, Jianyong Zheng, Chunyi Wang, Yifan Zhao, Liuying Chen

Control
03

MATHEMATICAL MODELLING · 2025

MCM / ICM Finalist Award

A sustainable tourism model bringing together NSGA-II, Sobol sensitivity analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation.

Project notes

Balancing tourism's economic, environmental, and social effects as a multi-objective decision problem. My role included lead paper writing, connecting the modelling choices, sensitivity analysis, and recommendations into a coherent research narrative.

Finalist ✳
✧
